customer_question: How do I rotate our live API key without downtime? We have about 12 services using it.
expert_resolution: Use Roll key in Dashboard > Developers > API keys. Relay creates a replacement key and lets you keep the old one active for up to 7 days. Deploy the new key to all 12 services during that window, confirm traffic on the new key in the API logs, then expire the old key early or let the overlap end. If any service still uses the old key after the overlap it will start receiving 401 invalid_api_key.

customer_question: Do you retry deliveries if our endpoint returns 404? We had a routing bug for an hour yesterday.
expert_resolution: Yes. Any response outside 200-299 counts as a failed attempt, including 404. Relay retries with exponential backoff (1 min, 5 min, 30 min, 2 h, 5 h, then every 10 h) for up to 15 attempts over about 3 days, so events from a one-hour routing bug will be redelivered automatically. You can confirm in Dashboard > Webhooks > Endpoint > Attempts. If you want them immediately, use bulk replay for that hour.

customer_question: Our handler takes about 20 seconds to process an order webhook and Relay keeps marking deliveries as failed, then sends the same event again. Why?
expert_resolution: Relay requires a 2xx response within 10 seconds. Your 20-second handler times out, so the attempt is marked failed (timeout) and retried, which is why you see the event again. Acknowledge immediately: put the event on a queue or background job, return 200 right away, and do the processing asynchronously. Also deduplicate on the event id, since retries can deliver the same event more than once.

customer_question: Signature verification with @relay/node 3.2.1 fails for some events but not others. We use express.raw and the correct endpoint secret. It seems to happen on events where the customer name has accents, like José.
expert_resolution: This is a known bug in @relay/node 3.2.0 to 3.2.2: webhooks.verify re-encodes string bodies as latin1, so any payload with non-ASCII characters (accents, emoji, CJK text) fails verification. Upgrade to @relay/node 3.2.3 or later. If you cannot upgrade right away, pass req.body as a Buffer instead of converting it to a string first. Your express.raw setup and secret are otherwise correct.

customer_question: Signature verification always fails in our Express app. We use express.json() and then JSON.stringify(req.body) before calling verify.
expert_resolution: Verification must use the raw request body exactly as Relay sent it. express.json() parses the body and JSON.stringify produces different whitespace and key formatting, so the HMAC never matches. Mount express.raw({ type: 'application/json' }) on the webhook route and pass req.body (a Buffer) straight to relay.webhooks.verify, then parse the returned event.

customer_question: We just created an account with EU data residency. Every API call returns 401 invalid_api_key, even with a brand new key.
expert_resolution: Accounts created with EU data residency live in the EU region and must call https://api.eu.relay.dev/v2 instead of api.relay.dev. EU keys are not valid on the global host, which is why you get 401 invalid_api_key. In the SDKs set the base URL: new Relay(key, { baseURL: 'https://api.eu.relay.dev/v2' }) in Node, or relay.Client(api_key=..., base_url='https://api.eu.relay.dev/v2') in Python.

customer_question: What happens when we exceed the rate limit? Is there a header that tells us how long to wait?
expert_resolution: Requests over the limit return 429 rate_limited with a Retry-After header giving the number of seconds to wait. The official SDKs already retry 429s with backoff up to 3 times. If you call the API directly, honor Retry-After and add jitter. Live mode allows 100 req/s and test mode 25 req/s per account, with short bursts up to 2x.

customer_question: Our endpoint stopped receiving any webhooks since Monday. The dashboard shows status disabled_failing. We fixed our server on Tuesday but still nothing arrives.
expert_resolution: Relay automatically disables an endpoint after 5 consecutive days of failed deliveries (status disabled_failing). Once disabled, new events are not attempted, and fixing the server does not re-enable it. Go to Dashboard > Webhooks > your endpoint and click Enable. Then run a bulk replay (POST /v2/events/replay with from and to) for the period the endpoint was failing so you receive what you missed; events are replayable for 30 days.

customer_question: Do retries count against our monthly event quota?
expert_resolution: No. Each event counts once toward your quota, regardless of how many endpoints receive it or how many retries it needs. Only live-mode events count; test-mode events are free.

customer_question: We send one event that fans out to 4 endpoints, and some deliveries need several retries. How many events are billed?
expert_resolution: One. Billing counts each event once, no matter how many endpoints it is delivered to or how many retry attempts it takes. Only live-mode events count toward the plan quota and overage.

customer_question: We got 409 idempotency_key_reused on POST /v2/events. What does it mean?
expert_resolution: You sent an Idempotency-Key that Relay already saw with a different request body or path within the last 24 hours. Relay refuses to guess which request you meant. Generate a new key whenever the request content changes, and only reuse a key when retrying the exact same request.

customer_question: We get 429s in test mode at around 10 requests per second, but your docs say the test limit is 25/s. Are the docs wrong?
expert_resolution: Test keys created before March 2024 are on a legacy rate-limit pool of 10 req/s. Roll your test key (Dashboard > Developers > API keys > Roll key) and the new key uses the current 25 req/s test limit. Live keys are not affected.

customer_question: We upgraded @relay/node from v2 to v3 and now verifyWebhook is undefined.
expert_resolution: In v3, verifyWebhook() moved to relay.webhooks.verify(rawBody, signatureHeader, secret), and relay.events.send() was renamed to relay.events.create(). Update both call sites. v2 only receives security fixes until 2025-12-31, so finishing the upgrade is the right move.

customer_question: Which IP addresses should we allowlist for webhook deliveries?
expert_resolution: Allow inbound HTTPS from 34.120.15.0/28 and 35.201.88.0/28. The current list is always available as JSON at https://api.relay.dev/v2/ips, and changes are announced at least 30 days in advance on the status page, so you can automate updates from that endpoint.

customer_question: We upgraded from Starter to Growth mid-month and the invoice shows two charges plus a negative line. Were we double charged?
expert_resolution: No double charge. When you upgrade mid-cycle the invoice shows a credit for the unused Starter time (the negative line) and a prorated Growth charge for the rest of the period; next month you will see only the Growth charge. If your finance team needs one consolidated invoice, email billing@relay.dev with the invoice number and we will issue a consolidated invoice.

customer_question: Valid-looking webhooks are rejected by our verification code with 'timestamp outside tolerance'. It only happens on one of our servers.
expert_resolution: The signature check rejects requests whose t timestamp is more than 300 seconds from your server's current time. If only one server fails, its clock has drifted by more than 5 minutes. Sync that server with NTP (for example chrony or systemd-timesyncd) and the same requests will verify.

customer_question: How do I replay all events from yesterday's outage window to one endpoint?
expert_resolution: Use bulk replay: POST /v2/events/replay with endpoint_id, from and to timestamps for the outage window, and optionally types. It runs in the background, handles up to 100,000 events per replay, and you can follow progress under Dashboard > Webhooks > Replays. Replays reuse the original event ids, so idempotent consumers skip anything already processed.

customer_question: All deliveries to our endpoint fail with 403 and the response body is an HTML page that says 'Just a moment...'. Our endpoint is behind Cloudflare.
expert_resolution: That HTML is Cloudflare's bot challenge. Cloudflare Bot Fight Mode (and Super Bot Fight Mode) challenges Relay deliveries because they are automated requests. On the Free plan Bot Fight Mode cannot be bypassed with WAF rules, so turn it off for the zone or move the webhook endpoint to a hostname without it. On Pro and higher, add a WAF custom rule that skips Super Bot Fight Mode for Relay's delivery ranges 34.120.15.0/28 and 35.201.88.0/28. Allowlisting the IPs in IP Access rules alone is not enough.

customer_question: Our account got paused and every API call returns 402 payment_required.
expert_resolution: Accounts are paused when an invoice is still unpaid 14 days after it was due; we retry the card 3 times over 7 days and email billing contacts first. Pay the open invoice or update the card in Dashboard > Settings > Billing. API access and deliveries resume as soon as the payment succeeds. Events sent while paused were rejected, so resend those from your side.

customer_question: If we retry POST /v2/events after a network timeout using the same Idempotency-Key the next day, will Relay deduplicate it?
expert_resolution: Only within 24 hours. Idempotency keys are stored for 24 hours; a retry with the same key after that is treated as a new request and can create a duplicate event. Retry promptly (the SDKs do this automatically), and for late retries check whether the event already exists or deduplicate on your own record id before resending.

customer_question: Using relay.AsyncClient in FastAPI, I get RuntimeError: Event loop is closed on the second request.
expert_resolution: relay-python 1.4.x binds AsyncClient's httpx connection pool to the event loop that is running when the client is created. If you create it at import time (module level) or in another loop, later requests fail with 'Event loop is closed'. Create the client inside FastAPI's lifespan handler (or use async with relay.AsyncClient() as client per task) and close it on shutdown. relay-python 1.5.0 fixes this by binding lazily to the running loop, so upgrading also resolves it.

customer_question: Our endpoint redirects to the www domain and every delivery fails with a 301.
expert_resolution: Relay does not follow redirects; any 3xx counts as a failed attempt. Update the endpoint URL in Dashboard > Webhooks to the final URL (including www and https) so it answers with 2xx directly. Failed events will be retried automatically, or you can bulk replay them.

customer_question: RelaySignatureError only on events that contain emoji in the payload. Node SDK v3.2.2.
expert_resolution: Known bug in @relay/node 3.2.0 to 3.2.2: verify re-encodes string bodies as latin1, which breaks payloads with emoji or other non-ASCII characters. Upgrade to 3.2.3 or later. Until then, pass the raw Buffer to relay.webhooks.verify instead of a string.

customer_question: How do I verify webhooks in Flask with relay-python?
expert_resolution: Pass the raw bytes, not the parsed JSON: event = relay.Webhook.verify(payload=request.get_data(), header=request.headers['Relay-Signature'], secret=WEBHOOK_SECRET). Do not use request.json before verifying. verify raises an error on an invalid signature or timestamp; return 400 in that case and 200 after successful handling.

customer_question: Can we rely on Relay delivering invoice.created before invoice.paid?
expert_resolution: No. Relay does not guarantee delivery order, and retries can make a later event arrive first. Make your handler order-independent: use the timestamps or a status field in the payload, or fetch the latest object state from your system when an event arrives, and deduplicate on the event id.

customer_question: We're on the Scale plan and need to replay events from 45 days ago after data loss on our side. The dashboard says the events are not replayable.
expert_resolution: Self-serve replay is limited to 30 days. Scale plan accounts can request an archive replay of events up to 90 days old: reply with the endpoint id, the UTC time range, and optional event types, and our team runs the archive replay, typically within 1 business day. Starter and Growth plans cannot replay beyond 30 days.

customer_question: The Python SDK returns invalid_api_key for our EU account key, but the same key works in the dashboard API explorer.
expert_resolution: EU data residency accounts must use the EU API host. Set base_url='https://api.eu.relay.dev/v2' on relay.Client (or AsyncClient). The dashboard explorer already targets the EU host, which is why the key works there and fails against the default global host.

customer_question: We are getting 403 mode_mismatch when updating an endpoint.
expert_resolution: mode_mismatch means the key and the object are in different modes: a test key (rk_test_) was used on a live endpoint or a live key (rk_live_) on a test endpoint. Use a key from the same mode as the endpoint. Test and live data never cross.

customer_question: Webhooks stopped after our staging server was down over the holidays. The server is back but no new attempts show in the log.
expert_resolution: Relay automatically disables an endpoint after 5 consecutive days of failed deliveries, so after the holiday outage your endpoint is in disabled_failing and new events are not attempted. Re-enable it in Dashboard > Webhooks > endpoint > Enable, then bulk replay the outage window (within 30 days) to receive the missed events.

customer_question: Our restricted key with webhooks:write gets 403 scope_insufficient when calling POST /v2/events/replay.
expert_resolution: Replay is an events operation, so it requires the events:write scope; webhooks:write only covers creating and updating endpoints. Edit the restricted key in Dashboard > Developers > API keys and add events:write, or create a dedicated key with events:write for your replay job. The required_scope field in the error body shows events:write.

customer_question: Deliveries to our new endpoint fail with tls_error in the attempt log.
expert_resolution: tls_error means Relay could not validate your endpoint's certificate. Relay requires TLS 1.2 or 1.3 and a certificate from a public CA that matches the hostname and is not expired. Self-signed or internal CA certificates are rejected. Check the chain with an SSL checker, install the full chain including intermediates, and retry.

customer_question: Calls to https://api.relay.dev/v1/events started returning 410 Gone.
expert_resolution: The v1 API was retired on 2024-06-30 and now returns 410. Switch to https://api.relay.dev/v2. If you use an SDK, upgrade to the current major version (Node v3 or the latest relay-python), which targets v2 by default.

customer_question: Signature verification fails on AWS Lambda behind API Gateway, but works locally.
expert_resolution: With API Gateway the body your Lambda receives is not always the raw bytes Relay signed. A non-proxy integration or mapping template re-serializes the JSON, and binary media types base64-encode the body (event.isBase64Encoded is true). Use Lambda proxy integration, and if isBase64Encoded is true decode event.body from base64 before verifying. Never parse and re-stringify the JSON before verifying.

customer_question: Can you add our VAT number to last month's invoice?
expert_resolution: Invoices are not reissued retroactively from the dashboard, so adding the VAT ID now only affects future invoices. Add it under Dashboard > Settings > Billing > Billing details so the next invoice includes it, and email billing@relay.dev with the invoice number and VAT ID to request a corrected copy of last month's invoice.

customer_question: Our CI load tests in test mode get rate limited much earlier than expected, around 10 requests per second.
expert_resolution: Test keys created before March 2024 are still on the legacy 10 req/s test pool. Roll the test key in Dashboard > Developers > API keys and use the new key in CI; it gets the current 25 req/s test limit.

customer_question: We get 413 when sending events that include large PDF attachments.
expert_resolution: Event payloads are limited to 256 KB and the limit cannot be raised. Do not embed files in events: upload the PDF to your storage and include a URL or file id in the payload, so consumers fetch the file when they process the event.

customer_question: We need to send about 300 events per second during a nightly sync in live mode, and we get 429s. What are our options?
expert_resolution: Live mode allows 100 requests per second per account, with short bursts up to 2x. Use POST /v2/events/batch to send up to 100 events per request, which brings 300 events/s down to a few requests per second. Spread the sync instead of starting it all at once. If you still need more, Scale plan accounts can request higher limits from their account manager.

customer_question: How do we change the timeout and number of retries in relay-python?
expert_resolution: Pass timeout (seconds, default 30) and max_retries (default 3) when creating the client: relay.Client(api_key=..., timeout=10, max_retries=5). The same options work on relay.AsyncClient. Set RELAY_LOG=debug to log each request and retry.

customer_question: Finance is asking why our invoice INV-2291 has three lines after the plan change. They need a single-line invoice for procurement.
expert_resolution: The three lines come from the mid-cycle upgrade: a credit for unused time on the old plan and a prorated charge for the new plan, plus the regular charge. The total is correct. Email billing@relay.dev with INV-2291 and we will issue a consolidated single-amount invoice for your procurement system.

customer_question: Is mutual TLS supported for webhook deliveries?
expert_resolution: Yes, on the Scale plan. Enable mTLS per endpoint, then download the Relay CA certificate from Dashboard > Settings > Security and configure your server to require client certificates signed by it. On other plans, verify the Relay-Signature header and optionally allowlist Relay's IP ranges.

customer_question: We want a key for our analytics service that can only read events. How do we set that up?
expert_resolution: Create a restricted key in Dashboard > Developers > API keys and select only the events:read scope. Any write call made with it will return 403 scope_insufficient, which is what you want for a read-only analytics service. Store it separately from your standard key.

customer_question: We allowlisted your IPs in Cloudflare but deliveries still fail with 403 and a challenge page.
expert_resolution: The challenge comes from Cloudflare Bot Fight Mode, which IP Access allowlisting does not bypass. On the Free plan turn Bot Fight Mode off for the zone (or use a hostname without it). On Pro and higher, add a WAF custom rule that skips Super Bot Fight Mode for 34.120.15.0/28 and 35.201.88.0/28.

customer_question: If we downgrade from Growth to Starter today, when does it take effect?
expert_resolution: Downgrades take effect at the start of your next billing period. You keep Growth limits until then, and the next invoice is at the Starter price. If your usage is above 1 million events next month, overage applies at $0.40 per 10,000 events.

customer_question: Celery task using asyncio.run with a module-level relay.AsyncClient fails on the second task with Event loop is closed.
expert_resolution: Each asyncio.run creates a new event loop, but relay-python 1.4.x binds the module-level AsyncClient to the first loop. Create the client inside the coroutine (async with relay.AsyncClient() as client) so it belongs to the current loop, or use the synchronous relay.Client in Celery. Upgrading to relay-python 1.5.0 also fixes it.

customer_question: Which scope do we need for bulk replay? Our ops tool key has webhooks:read and webhooks:write.
expert_resolution: Bulk replay needs events:write. The webhooks scopes only cover endpoint management. Add events:write to the ops tool's restricted key in Dashboard > Developers > API keys.

customer_question: We see the same event id delivered twice to our endpoint. Is that a bug?
expert_resolution: No. Relay delivers at least once, so retries (for example after a timeout where your server actually processed the request) can deliver the same event more than once. Store processed event ids and skip ones you have seen. Responding within 10 seconds with a 2xx reduces duplicates.

customer_question: After upgrading @relay/node from 3.1 to 3.2.0, roughly 5% of our webhooks fail verification. Nothing else changed.
expert_resolution: @relay/node 3.2.0 to 3.2.2 has a bug that breaks verification for payloads containing non-ASCII characters, which matches your ~5%. Upgrade to 3.2.3 or later, or pass the raw Buffer to verify until you can upgrade.

customer_question: Can we get events from two months ago redelivered? We are a Scale customer, endpoint ep_9x2.
expert_resolution: Yes. Self-serve replay only covers 30 days, but Scale accounts can request an archive replay for events up to 90 days old. Send the UTC time range and any event types for ep_9x2 and we will run it, usually within 1 business day.

customer_question: We moved to the EU region last week and our integration broke with 401s.
expert_resolution: After moving to the EU region your account is served from https://api.eu.relay.dev/v2. Calls to api.relay.dev return 401 invalid_api_key for EU keys. Update the base URL in your SDK configuration or HTTP client.

customer_question: Lambda function URL: verify fails, and event.body looks like random base64.
expert_resolution: When event.isBase64Encoded is true the body is base64 encoded. Decode it (Buffer.from(event.body, 'base64')) and pass the decoded bytes to relay.webhooks.verify. Do not parse the JSON before verifying.

customer_question: We rolled our endpoint signing secret. Will requests signed with the old secret still verify?
expert_resolution: For 24 hours after rolling, Relay signs each delivery with both secrets and sends two v1 values in Relay-Signature. Accept a request if either v1 matches, deploy the new secret within the 24 hours, and then remove the old one.

customer_question: Why did Relay stop retrying? Our endpoint returned 500 for about a week after a bad deploy, and now there are no new attempts at all even though it is fixed.
expert_resolution: Two things happened. Each event is retried for up to 15 attempts over about 3 days, and after 5 consecutive days of failures Relay automatically disabled the endpoint (disabled_failing), so new events are not attempted either. Re-enable the endpoint in Dashboard > Webhooks, then bulk replay the week of the bad deploy (within the 30-day window).

customer_question: Webhooks to our Cloudflare-proxied domain fail with non_2xx 403. Sending directly to the origin works.
expert_resolution: Cloudflare Bot Fight Mode is challenging Relay deliveries before they reach your origin. Turn it off for the zone on the Free plan, or on Pro and higher add a WAF custom rule that skips Super Bot Fight Mode for Relay's delivery ranges 34.120.15.0/28 and 35.201.88.0/28.

customer_question: We added a mapping template in API Gateway to pass headers through, and now every signature fails.
expert_resolution: A mapping template makes API Gateway re-serialize the body, so it no longer matches the bytes Relay signed. Switch the route to Lambda proxy integration (headers are passed through automatically) and verify the raw event.body, base64-decoding it first if isBase64Encoded is true.

customer_question: We cancelled our Growth plan mid-month. Will we get a refund for the remaining days?
expert_resolution: No. Relay does not refund partial months. After cancelling, your Growth plan stays active until the end of the paid period, and you will not be charged again.

customer_question: Test-mode 429 errors started when we added a second CI runner. Combined we only do about 12 requests per second.
expert_resolution: Two factors: rate limits are shared across all keys in the same account and mode, and test keys created before March 2024 are on a legacy 10 req/s pool. Roll the test key so both runners use a key on the current 25 req/s test limit.

customer_question: 403 scope_insufficient when replaying single events from our admin panel.
expert_resolution: Replaying an event, single or bulk, requires the events:write scope. Your admin panel's restricted key is missing it. Add events:write to the key in Dashboard > Developers > API keys.

customer_question: The upgrade last week created an invoice with a credit line. Can you make it one line?
expert_resolution: The credit is the unused time on your previous plan and the second line is the prorated new plan, so the total is correct. Email billing@relay.dev with the invoice number and we will issue a consolidated invoice with a single amount.

customer_question: pytest-asyncio: the first test passes, the rest fail with RuntimeError Event loop is closed. relay-python 1.4.2.
expert_resolution: pytest-asyncio gives each test a new event loop, but relay-python 1.4.x binds AsyncClient to the loop where it was created. Create the client in a function-scoped async fixture (async with relay.AsyncClient() as client: yield client), or upgrade to relay-python 1.5.0, which binds lazily to the running loop.

customer_question: The bulk replay API returns an error for a range older than 30 days. Is there any way around it for Scale?
expert_resolution: The API and dashboard are limited to 30 days. Scale accounts can request an archive replay for up to 90 days: send the endpoint id, UTC range and event types to support and we run it, typically within 1 business day.

customer_question: We're on @relay/node 3.2.1 and verify() throws RelaySignatureError for orders from our Japanese storefront. Orders from the US store verify fine. Same endpoint and secret.
expert_resolution: This is the known @relay/node 3.2.0 to 3.2.2 bug with non-ASCII payloads; Japanese product names trigger it. Upgrade to @relay/node 3.2.3 or later. Until then, pass the raw Buffer to relay.webhooks.verify instead of a string. Your secret and endpoint are fine.

customer_question: Signatures verify in our local Express server but fail after deploying to Lambda with an API Gateway REST API. Same secret.
expert_resolution: API Gateway is changing the body before your code sees it. With a non-proxy integration or mapping template it re-serializes the JSON; with binary media types it base64-encodes it. Use Lambda proxy integration and verify event.body, decoding it from base64 first when isBase64Encoded is true.

customer_question: Since last Thursday our production endpoint receives nothing. The attempts tab is empty for new events and the endpoint badge is red. Our endpoint returns 200 when we curl it ourselves.
expert_resolution: Your endpoint was automatically disabled (disabled_failing) after 5 consecutive days of failed deliveries, so Relay stopped attempting new events. A working endpoint does not re-enable it automatically. Click Enable in Dashboard > Webhooks > endpoint, then bulk replay from the first failure until now (within 30 days) to receive what you missed.

customer_question: Our integration test suite hits rate_limited in test mode at roughly 10 requests per second. Our account is from 2023. Live mode is fine.
expert_resolution: Test keys created before March 2024 are on a legacy 10 req/s rate-limit pool. Roll your test key in Dashboard > Developers > API keys and use the new key in the test suite; it gets the current 25 req/s test limit. Live keys are unaffected.

customer_question: We moved from Starter to Growth on the 12th. The invoice has a -$30 line and a $203 line. Our AP team says it looks like a duplicate charge and wants a single invoice amount for their system.
expert_resolution: It is not a duplicate. The -$30 line is the credit for unused Starter time and the $203 line is the prorated Growth charge for the rest of the period. Next month you will see only the Growth charge. Email billing@relay.dev with the invoice number and we will issue a consolidated invoice with a single amount for your AP system.

customer_question: Brand new account; we chose EU data residency for GDPR. Our first curl to api.relay.dev/v2/events returns 401 invalid_api_key. The key was copied directly from the dashboard.
expert_resolution: EU data residency accounts must call the EU host: https://api.eu.relay.dev/v2. Keys from EU accounts are rejected by the global api.relay.dev host with 401 invalid_api_key. Change the URL in your curl and SDK configuration and the same key will work.

customer_question: Every attempt in the log shows 403, and the stored response body is HTML containing cf-chl. We already added Relay's IP ranges to our Cloudflare IP Access rules.
expert_resolution: cf-chl is Cloudflare's challenge page from Bot Fight Mode, and IP Access rules do not bypass Bot Fight Mode. On the Free plan turn Bot Fight Mode off for the zone or move the endpoint to a hostname without it. On Pro and higher, add a WAF custom rule that skips Super Bot Fight Mode for 34.120.15.0/28 and 35.201.88.0/28.

customer_question: Our aiohttp worker creates one relay.AsyncClient at startup in a global. The first batch of events sends fine, then every call raises RuntimeError: Event loop is closed. relay-python 1.4.3.
expert_resolution: relay-python 1.4.x binds AsyncClient to the event loop that exists when it is created. Your global client is created before the worker's running loop (or the loop is replaced), so later calls fail. Create the client inside the worker's startup hook on the running loop and close it on cleanup, or upgrade to relay-python 1.5.0, which binds lazily.

customer_question: Our warehouse lost about 50 days of order events in a migration. We're on Scale. The bulk replay API rejects our date range. Is there any way to get these redelivered?
expert_resolution: Yes. Self-serve replay stops at 30 days, but Scale accounts can request an archive replay for events up to 90 days old. Send us the endpoint id, the UTC time range and any event types, and we will run the archive replay, typically within 1 business day.

customer_question: Our on-call tool uses a restricted key with webhooks:read, webhooks:write and events:read. Replaying a failed event returns 403. What's missing?
expert_resolution: Replaying requires events:write. events:read only allows reading events, and the webhooks scopes only cover endpoint management. Add events:write to the on-call tool's restricted key in Dashboard > Developers > API keys.
